Your server asks Tegata for a **checkout session** with the price, sends the customer to it (or opens it over your
page with [Checkout](/docs/build/checkout)), and gets a signed **webhook** when NEAR has settled the payment. The
business receives exactly the amount, in USDC on NEAR.

<Steps>
<Step>
### Make a key

In the app, **Developers** → **New key**. Copy it: it's shown only once.
</Step>
<Step>
### Add a webhook endpoint

Your https URL, or **Use Tegata's test inbox** to watch webhooks arrive without a server.
</Step>
<Step>
### Create a session per order

`POST /api/v1/checkout/sessions` with the amount and your order in `metadata`. Send the customer to its `url`.
</Step>
<Step>
### Fulfil on `checkout.session.completed`

Check the signature, find your order in `data.metadata`, ship it. (Your own counter sales send this event too, without
your order in their metadata.)
</Step>
</Steps>

<Shot src="/shots/wide/app-developers.webp" alt="The Developers page: Create a checkout session with the curl and Copy; API keys with Shop server and Revoke; Webhooks with Tegata's test inbox, its switch, Send test event, Reveal secret and Remove, Add endpoint and the four event chips; the Test inbox with checkout.session.completed and payment.succeeded, each Signature valid" caption="Developers in the app: the quickstart, your keys, your endpoints and the test inbox." address="tegata.xyz/app/developers" />

## API keys

**New key** asks for a name ("Shop server") and shows the key once: "Copy it now. It's shown only once." Tegata keeps
only its SHA-256 hash. The list shows each key's first characters and when it was last used, with **Revoke**; a
revoked key stops working at once. Creating a key emails the owner a security notice.

| Made in | Starts with | Works on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Sandbox | `tk_test_` | NEAR testnet, test USDC |
| Live | `tk_live_` | NEAR mainnet, real USDC |

Keep keys on your server. Anyone with one can create sessions for your business.

## Requests

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Base URL | `https://tegata.xyz/api/v1` |
| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer tk_test_…` on every request |
| Body | JSON, with `Content-Type: application/json` |
| Amounts | Dollars as display strings (`"25.00"`, `"1,250.00"`), and the same in USDC base units (`"25000000"`, 6 decimals): do your sums with `amount_units` |

| Endpoint | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /checkout/sessions` | Create a checkout session |
| `GET /checkout/sessions/{id}` | Read one back |
| `GET /events?limit=20` | The latest events, newest first |

Errors are JSON with a code and a sentence you can show:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "bad_input", "message": "amount must be between 0.01 and 1000000" } }
```

| Status | `code` | For example (real answers) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` | `unauthorized` | "Send your API key as Authorization: Bearer tk_…" · "That API key isn't valid, or was revoked" |
| `400` | `bad_input` | "amount must look like 25 or 25.50 (dollars)" · "amount must be between 0.01 and 1000000" · "success_url must be an https URL" · "metadata holds at most 20 keys" |
| `400` | `invalid` | A field of the wrong type or length: "Too big: expected string to have &lt;=80 characters" |
| `404` | `not_found` | "No such session" (not yours, or no such id) |
| `409` | `not_ready` | "The business's account is still being set up" |
| `500` | `server_error` | "Something went wrong on our side". Today this is also what a body that isn't valid JSON gets |

There's no request rate limit in the code today.

## Checkout sessions

A session is a one-time payment for an exact amount, paid on Tegata's pay page. It's paid once, in full.

### Create one

```bash
curl https://tegata.xyz/api/v1/checkout/sessions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEGATA_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: order-1042" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount": "1.00", "description": "Order #1042",
       "success_url": "https://docs.tegata.xyz/demo-shop",
       "metadata": {"order": "1042"}}'
```

| Field | Takes |
| --- | --- |
| `amount` | Required. Dollars: `"25"`, `"25.50"` or `25.5`, from 0.01 to 1,000,000 |
| `description` | What the payer sees on the page and the receipt. Up to 80 characters; "Checkout" if empty |
| `success_url` | An https address (or `localhost`), up to 500 characters. Once paid, the page shows **Back to** your business, linking there |
| `metadata` | Up to 20 keys, each value a string of up to 500 characters. Comes back on the session and in its webhook |

**`Idempotency-Key`** (a header; longer than 200 characters, it's cut to 200): once a body has passed the checks
above, the same key from the same API key returns the session it made the first time, whatever the body says, so a
retry never makes a second one.

The reply is `201`. This one is real, from the Sandbox, made with the call above on 13 Nov 2026:

```json
{
  "id": "80283455-f180-459c-8003-84f81225d6f8",
  "object": "checkout.session",
  "status": "open",
  "url": "https://tegata.xyz/pay/zFydXvEnyZjFzF",
  "amount": "1.00",
  "amount_units": "1000000",
  "currency": "usd",
  "settlement": { "asset": "USDC", "network": "near-testnet", "account": "studio-kaze-5601a94a.testnet" },
  "description": "Order #1042",
  "success_url": "https://docs.tegata.xyz/demo-shop",
  "metadata": { "order": "1042" },
  "payment": null,
  "created_at": "2026-11-13T16:22:48.698Z"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | `open` until paid; `complete` once paid in full. Sessions have no timer: one you create stays open until it's paid. (`expired` is a session closed unpaid; today only a cancelled [counter](/docs/guide/counter) sale becomes one) |
| `url` | The pay page. Send the customer there, or open it over your page with `data-tegata-session` or `Tegata.checkout({ session })` |
| `amount`, `amount_units` | The price in dollars, and in USDC base units |
| `settlement` | Where the money lands: USDC, `near-testnet` or `near-mainnet`, and the business's account |
| `payment` | `null` until paid; then the [payment](#the-payment-object). A fully refunded payment drops back to `null`, while `status` stays `complete` |

### Read it back

```bash
curl https://tegata.xyz/api/v1/checkout/sessions/80283455-f180-459c-8003-84f81225d6f8 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEGATA_KEY"
```

The same object, now. A key reads sessions of its business in either mode. Once it's paid, `status` is `complete` and `payment` is filled in. This is a real paid one, from
the [proof run](#a-real-one) below (on the app at `localhost`):

```json
{
  "id": "2f852836-9206-492e-9d6e-830148366c96",
  "object": "checkout.session",
  "status": "complete",
  "url": "http://localhost:3100/pay/E32DvMBiifrjmx",
  "amount": "0.25",
  "amount_units": "250000",
  "currency": "usd",
  "settlement": { "asset": "USDC", "network": "near-testnet", "account": "dev-eee78deb.tegata.testnet" },
  "description": "Order #1042",
  "success_url": "https://shop.example/thanks",
  "metadata": { "order": "1042" },
  "payment": {
    "id": "35fc8d8f-dabe-4c8f-9302-d37e1389b34c",
    "object": "payment",
    "amount": "0.25",
    "amount_units": "250000",
    "refunded_units": "0",
    "currency": "usd",
    "rail": "near_wallet",
    "payer": "customer-eab2310f.tegata.testnet",
    "network": "near-testnet",
    "tx_hash": "6tmnGKULQVyUUeGdpWNQYLNWCrCCmiv4iqQtsimSnBnF",
    "request_id": "2f852836-9206-492e-9d6e-830148366c96",
    "settled_at": "2026-11-13T07:23:50.807Z"
  },
  "created_at": "2026-11-13T07:23:30.520Z"
}
```

### The payment object

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The payment |
| `amount`, `amount_units` | What was paid, in dollars and in USDC base units |
| `refunded_units` | How much has been refunded so far |
| `rail` | How it was paid: `tegata` (a Tegata balance), `near_wallet`, `oneclick` (another chain, through NEAR Intents), `card` (Transak), or `manual` (marked paid by hand) |
| `payer` | Who paid, as Tegata knows it: a NEAR account; for another chain, the payer's refund address there; for `manual`, the owner's note, if any |
| `network` | `near-testnet` or `near-mainnet` |
| `tx_hash` | The NEAR transaction that settled it (none for `manual`) |
| `request_id` | The session, pay link or invoice it paid |
| `settled_at` | When Tegata read it as final on NEAR |

## Events

```bash
curl "https://tegata.xyz/api/v1/events?limit=2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEGATA_KEY"
```

The latest events for the key's mode, newest first: `limit` from 1 to 100 (20 by default). Each is the same body a
webhook carries:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "52f9ec3b-c783-44ad-bddf-d4696b541c47",
      "type": "checkout.session.completed",
      "created_at": "2026-11-13T08:31:04.535Z",
      "data": { "id": "b2be9dca-…", "object": "checkout.session", "status": "complete", "amount": "0.10",
                "metadata": { "order": "1042" }, "payment": { "rail": "near_wallet", "tx_hash": "c9Wndd…", "…": "…" } }
    },
    {
      "id": "6f6bb447-4172-4b09-b70c-0d8a58712c5d",
      "type": "payment.succeeded",
      "created_at": "2026-11-13T08:31:04.535Z",
      "data": { "id": "db4d30cb-…", "object": "payment", "amount": "0.10", "rail": "near_wallet", "…": "…" }
    }
  ]
}
```

That's Studio Kaze's real Order #1042 in the Sandbox.

## Webhooks

Add endpoints in **Developers**: type an https URL and press **Add endpoint**, or **Use Tegata's test inbox**. Each
endpoint gets its own signing secret (`whsec_…`), shown once and behind **Reveal secret** after that. Every endpoint
gets every event of its mode. A switch turns one off; **Remove** deletes it.

| Rule | |
| --- | --- |
| URL | https only, and never an address inside a private network (checked on add and on every send). On a self-hosted development server (not in production), `ALLOW_LOCAL_WEBHOOKS=true` allows `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` |
| Endpoints | Up to 5 in each mode |
| Success | Any 2xx within 10 seconds. Redirects are not followed |
| Retries | About 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 1 h and 6 h after each failure (a sweep picks them up every minute): six tries in all, then the delivery is marked failed and the owner gets an email ("Your webhook to … is failing"), at most once a day per endpoint |

### Events

| `type` | Sent when | `data` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checkout.session.completed` | A session is paid in full, including your own [counter](/docs/guide/counter) sales (their `metadata` is `{ "source": "counter" }`) | The session's `id`, `object`, `status`, `amount`, `amount_units`, `currency`, `description`, `success_url`, `metadata` and `payment` (no `url`, `settlement` or `created_at`) |
| `payment.succeeded` | Any payment to the business settles: a session, a pay link (and so a Checkout button), an invoice, a counter sale, money marked paid by hand, or the owner adding money from another chain or a card | The [payment](#the-payment-object) |
| `payment.refunded` | The business refunds a payment, all or part | The payment, plus `refund_units` and `refund_tx` |
| `invoice.paid` | An invoice is paid in full | `{ id, object: "invoice", number, amount, amount_units, currency, request_id }` |
| `ping` | **Send test event**, to that one endpoint if it's switched on | `{ object: "ping", message: "Hello from Tegata", endpoint_id }`. Pings show in `GET /events` too |

A payment and its events are written in the same database transaction, so one never exists without the other. Each
event is stored once.

### What arrives

```http
POST /tegata/webhooks HTTP/1.1
content-type: application/json
user-agent: Tegata-Webhooks/1
webhook-id: msg_<delivery id>
webhook-timestamp: <unix seconds>
webhook-signature: v1,<base64 signature>

{"id":"838bc31c-…","type":"checkout.session.completed","created_at":"2026-11-13T07:23:50.806Z","data":{…}}
```

The headers are [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com). `webhook-id` stays the same across the retries
of one delivery, and across a **Resend** of it too: store it to ignore repeats, and make fulfilment safe to run twice
if you also want a Resend to count. The timestamp is fresh on every try.

### Check the signature

Always against the raw body, as a string, before you parse it.

<Tabs items={["Node (library)", "Node (no library)", "Python"]}>
<Tab value="Node (library)">

```js
import { Webhook } from "standardwebhooks" // npm i standardwebhooks

const wh = new Webhook(process.env.TEGATA_WEBHOOK_SECRET) // whsec_…

// rawBody: the request body exactly as it arrived, as a string
const event = wh.verify(rawBody, {
  "webhook-id": req.headers["webhook-id"],
  "webhook-timestamp": req.headers["webhook-timestamp"],
  "webhook-signature": req.headers["webhook-signature"],
}) // throws if it's wrong or more than 5 minutes off

if (event.type === "checkout.session.completed" && event.data.metadata.order) fulfil(event.data.metadata.order)
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Node (no library)">

```js
import crypto from "node:crypto"

export function verifyTegataWebhook(rawBody, headers, secret) {
  const id = headers["webhook-id"]
  const timestamp = headers["webhook-timestamp"]
  const signatures = headers["webhook-signature"]
  if (!id || !timestamp || !signatures) throw new Error("Missing webhook headers")
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(timestamp)) > 5 * 60) throw new Error("Too old or too new")
  const key = Buffer.from(secret.replace(/^whsec_/, ""), "base64")
  const expected = crypto.createHmac("sha256", key).update(`${id}.${timestamp}.${rawBody}`).digest("base64")
  const ok = signatures.split(" ").some((entry) => {
    const [version, signature] = entry.split(",")
    return version === "v1" && signature?.length === expected.length &&
      crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(signature), Buffer.from(expected))
  })
  if (!ok) throw new Error("Bad signature")
  return JSON.parse(rawBody)
}
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">

```python
import base64, hashlib, hmac, json, time

def verify_tegata_webhook(raw_body: bytes, headers: dict, secret: str) -> dict:
    msg_id = headers["webhook-id"]
    timestamp = headers["webhook-timestamp"]
    signatures = headers["webhook-signature"]
    if abs(time.time() - int(timestamp)) > 5 * 60:
        raise ValueError("Too old or too new")
    key = base64.b64decode(secret.removeprefix("whsec_"))
    signed = f"{msg_id}.{timestamp}.".encode() + raw_body
    expected = base64.b64encode(hmac.new(key, signed, hashlib.sha256).digest()).decode()
    for entry in signatures.split(" "):
        version, _, signature = entry.partition(",")
        if version == "v1" and hmac.compare_digest(signature, expected):
            return json.loads(raw_body)
    raise ValueError("Bad signature")
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

The signature is `v1,` and a base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `webhook-id.webhook-timestamp.body`, keyed with the secret after
`whsec_`, base64-decoded. All three versions above were checked against signatures made the way Tegata makes them.

### The test inbox, Send test event, the log

- **Use Tegata's test inbox** adds an endpoint that Tegata hosts. It checks each webhook's signature, and the **Test
  inbox** list shows the latest 10 arrivals with "Signature valid" or "Bad signature": the whole loop, before you
  write a handler.
- **Send test event** sends a `ping` to that endpoint now (if it's switched on).
- **Deliveries** lists the latest 30: the event, the endpoint and **Delivered** with the status code, **Retrying**
  with the number of tries, **Failed** or **Sending**. Open one to see its payload; **Resend** sends it again from the
  first try.

## The app's own endpoints

The app itself talks to `/api/…` routes signed in as the owner (the email sign-in's token, or a NEAR-wallet session),
not with an API key. They aren't the public API and may change, but here is what a few of them take, so you know how
the screens work:

| Endpoint | Body | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/pots` | | The split rule (`on`, `taxBps`, `savingsBps`), `tax`, `savings`, `spendable` and `balance` in USDC base units, and the latest moves. See [Pots](/docs/guide/balance#pots-tax-and-savings) |
| `PATCH /api/pots` | `{ "on": true, "taxBps": 2500, "savingsBps": 1000 }` | Sets the split. Basis points, whole percentages from 0 to 90, together at most 90% |
| `POST /api/pots/move` | `{ "kind": "tax", "direction": "to_spending", "amount": "50" }` | Moves between a pot and spending (`to_spending` or `to_pot`), up to what the pot holds or what's spendable |
| `POST /api/people`, `PATCH /api/people/{id}` | `{ "name": "Kofi Mensah", "email": "…", "role": "Engineer", "amount": "3100", "kind": "contractor" }` | Adds or edits a person. `kind` is `employee` (the default) or `contractor`; left out on an edit, it stays as it was. See [Pay people](/docs/guide/pay-people#add-your-team) |
| `PUT /api/payroll/runs/{id}/rows/{rowId}` | `{ "pay": "2850" or null, "lines": [{ "kind": "bonus", "label": "Q4 target", "amount": "250" }] }` | This run's pay for one person (`null` keeps their usual pay) and up to 10 lines, `bonus`, `reimbursement` or `deduction`, while the run is a draft. See [This run's pay](/docs/guide/pay-people#this-runs-pay) |

## A real one

`packages/services/src/proofs/developers.ts` runs the whole loop on NEAR testnet, with the app and the worker
running:

1. A business gets an API key, and Tegata's test inbox as its endpoint.
2. A real `curl` creates the session above. The same `Idempotency-Key` sent again returns the same session.
3. A customer with its own NEAR account pays it the way a NEAR wallet does: <Tx hash="6tmnGKULQVyUUeGdpWNQYLNWCrCCmiv4iqQtsimSnBnF" />.
4. The worker reads the USDC transfer from NEAR, marks the session complete and sends `payment.succeeded` and
   `checkout.session.completed`. Both arrive at the inbox with valid signatures and a `200`.
5. A second `curl` reads the session back as `complete`, with the transaction hash.

The session was created at 07:23:30 and paid at 07:23:50.

<Callout title="Sandbox and Live">
  A `tk_test_` key makes sessions on NEAR testnet; switch to Live and a `tk_live_` key makes them on NEAR mainnet,
  where a customer can also pay a session from another chain through NEAR Intents (or by card, once Transak's keys are
  set). The proof above is on testnet; Live has no recorded payment yet.
</Callout>
